sections.title: New Media and Politics
sections.description:
How do emerging media technologies reshape political power, public opinion, and democratic participation? This course explores one of the most consequential transformations in contemporary politics: the rise of digital media and its impact on elections, governance, journalism, and civic life.
Drawing from political communication theories, media studies, and campaign strategy, students will explore the evolution of the American media environment from the rise of  radio and television in the early to mid-20th century to the introduction of the internet into presidential campaigns in 1996 and the subsequent emergence of social media, platform politics, and artificial intelligence as forces shaping contemporary democracy. Particular attention will be given to the role of social media platforms, podcasts, online influencers, and artificial intelligence in shaping political discourse, mobilizing voters, influencing public opinion, and redefining the relationship between citizens and political institutions.
The course combines historical analysis with real-time examination of current events, including the aftermath of the 2026 midterm elections, the remaining presidential term of  Donald Trump, and the emerging dynamics of the 2028 presidential race. Students will critically assess questions surrounding misinformation and disinformation, political persuasion, campaign advertising, public opinion measurement, and election law all operating in a fragmented information ecosystem.
